🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN-HABITAT CROWNS CDMX'S UTOPÍAS</u>

Mexico City mayor Clara Brugada received UN-Habitat's Scroll of Honour, the agency's top award for urban innovation, from executive director Anacláudia Rossbach on Sunday, at the opening of UTOPÍA La Soberana in Gustavo A. Madero. It is the biggest one yet: 300 million pesos turning the old Deportivo Hermanos Galeana, 91,377 m², into 80 spaces for care, health, culture and sport. The UN says the model is already inspiring projects in Quito. Brugada calls the Utopías "factories of equality."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM TO LULA: "THE PEOPLE WON"</u>

President Sheinbaum congratulated Lula da Silva on his re-election Sunday night: "Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won. Congratulations, President Lula!" Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro 51.76% to 48.24% in a runoff where a judge ordered the arrest of a Bolsonaro-allied official in Salvador de Bahia for holding back public buses on election day, and the electoral court extended voting by two hours. Latin America's two largest economies remain in progressive hands.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE CHIEF TADDEI RESIGNS</u>

Guadalupe Taddei announced Sunday she will hand her resignation as president of Mexico's National Electoral Institute to the Chamber of Deputies on Monday. Two days ago she was vowing not to back down. Since then, the federal auditor (ASF) reported signs of irregular contracts, conflicts of interest, collusion and triangulated funds, and videos surfaced showing her family's closeness to an electoral-materials supplier. Her statement says protecting the institute must come before any personal interest.

🔥🇲🇽 "We cannot forget that era of handing over public resources, public companies, to a few, and then those few decided to govern Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Morelia, Michoacán At the Morelia housing handover she recalled the neoliberal period, 1982–2018. Teléfonos de México, mines, banks, cement, petrochemical and fertilizer plants, highways and steel mills all belonged to the people. Before Salinas, one Mexican family was on the world's list of the very rich; when he left, 40 were. She said Raúl Salinas de Gortari lent Ricardo Salinas Pliego the money to buy the state broadcaster Imevisión, today TV Azteca. Then came the 1994 crisis, private bank debts turned into public debt, the fraud of 2006, and the privatizations of Pemex and the CFE, while the minimum wage did not rise for 36 years.
